ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Applicable statutes include the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), Act No. 6516, as amended, and its Enforcement Decree; the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Secrecy, Act No. 5493, as amended; the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Articles 287-2 through 287-30 governing Yuhan Hoesa; and the Financial Services Commission/FIU customer due diligence and beneficial owner identification regulations implementing FATF standards. Beneficial owner information is not disclosed to the public but is reported to the Korean FIU and relevant supervisory authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Matters / Company Registration Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Commercial Registry via the Supreme Court of Korea e-Registry Service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the destination state is a member of the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, the sole authentication route is issuance of an Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) Apostille Section; no consular legalization step is added. If the destination state is a non-member, the sole route is MOFA Consular Bureau certification followed by legalization at the destination country's Embassy or Consulate in Seoul. The Apostille and consular routes are parallel and mutually exclusive, never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Business Registration Certificate and Tax Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea and the competent District Tax Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: obtain the official NTS certificate, then obtain a single Apostille from MOFA. Consular route: obtain the official NTS certificate, have MOFA certify it, then have the destination embassy or consulate legalize it. Use only the route required by the destination jurisdiction; Apostille and consular legalization are alternatives and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for incorporation and foreign filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial directors and shareholders of Yuhan Hoesa, executed before and notarized by a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized original is required before authentication. Apostille route: notarization followed by MOFA Apostille issuance. Consular route: notarization followed by MOFA Consular Bureau certification and then destination embassy or consulate legalization. These routes are mutually exclusive and no document should receive both an Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jungwan) of Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa shareholders and directors, notarized by a Korean Notary Public and filed with the District Court Commercial Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: notarized articles followed by MOFA Apostille. Consular route: notarized articles followed by MOFA Consular Bureau certification and then destination embassy or consulate legalization. The two authentication paths are parallel and exclusive; sequential chaining is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Corporate Banking Relationship Confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed commercial bank, after account opening and KYC compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: if required, have the bank officer signature and corporate seal notarized, then obtain a MOFA Apostille. Consular route: if required, notarize the signature and seal, then obtain MOFA Consular Bureau certification followed by destination embassy or consulate legalization. No document shall receive both Apostille and consular legalization; only the mandated route applies.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory protocol requires real-time screening of all direct and indirect shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, counterparties, customers, and vessel/aircraft parties against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list and OFAC 50% Rule, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and the Republic of Korea's financial sanctions and restricted designations issued by the Financial Services Commission, the FIU, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Enhanced due diligence, verified source-of-funds documentation, and senior management approval are mandatory for any person identified as a Politically Exposed Person, family member, close associate, or any person located in or transacting with a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction. All screening results must be dated, evidenced, and retained for at least five years under FTRA record-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry (Internet Registration Office) and the Commercial Chamber of the District Court Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in the Korean alphabet (Hangul) and must include the Yuhan Hoesa corporate-form suffix. A parallel English trade name is permitted for international contracts, but the Korean court registry and tax authority treat the Hangul name as the primary registered name. Phonetic transliteration of foreign words into Hangul is allowed where the resulting name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name. The registry applies a four-part name structure: distinctive proprietary element, business-purpose descriptive element, corporate-form suffix, and registered place-of-business locality, all of which must be set out in the incorporation application.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the filer must first identify the legal ground stated in the registry rejection notice. Within one week, the filer should file a written correction or re-submission accompanied by a revised name certificate, a fresh clearance search, and, where applicable, prior ministerial approval. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act before the competent appellate court, and thereafter may seek administrative litigation in the Administrative Court within the statutory limitation period. The appeal must attach the rejection notice, proof of fee payment, and legal argument demonstrating distinctive name comparability and absence of confusion.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-box-only address is not permissible for this Yuhan Hoesa operating in ISIC 5229 dangerous-goods freight forwarding. The National Tax Service requires a physical place of business evidenced by an original lease contract before issuing a business registration certificate, and Korea Customs Service, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and banks require physical office presence, a local responsible manager, operational records, and an in-person KYC interview. A mail-only address will be rejected by tax authorities, the corporate registry, and financial institutions, and will fail commercial-substance testing for the DG freight forwarding license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is high, approximately 80-90% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, increasing after VAT registration and DG license application. Mandatory checklist: original or notarized lease agreement; visible nameplate in the Korean legal name; local manager and employment records; accounting books, tax invoices, and customs broker or freight forwarding license; dangerous-goods handling permits; functioning telephone and email channels; and no evidence of sub-letting or mail-only arrangements. Inspections are conducted by the National Tax Service, municipal tax offices, Korea Customs Service, and transport safety authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-42 (Limited Liability Company, Yuhan Hoesa); Commercial Registration Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Corporate Tax Act; Value Added Tax Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office address, operating through the Supreme Court Electronic Registration System (IRO) and the online commercial registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Commercial registration application for the incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation and the certificate of capital subscription payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa and no blocked escrow account is required. Subscribers may fix the stated capital in the Articles of Incorporation, and capital may be subscribed in cash or in kind. Foreign currency contributions must be received through an authorized foreign exchange bank; the bank must issue a certificate of deposit of capital for use in the commercial registration filing. In-kind contributions require an independent valuation when the stated capital is subscribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE YUHAN HOESA. The undersigned initial director, acting jointly with the incorporators and shareholders, hereby records the following formal resolutions adopted at the first meeting of the board. 1. Share Capital Subscription and Allotment. The board adopts the pro-forma subscription list and authorizes the issuance of the stated paid-up capital of the company as set out in the Articles of Incorporation. Each subscriber is recorded as having contributed the amount shown opposite the subscriber’s name, and the board confirms that the capital has been duly paid into the company’s bank subscription account or, in the case of in-kind contribution, properly valued and transferred. 2. Banking Authorization. The board authorizes the opening of corporate operating, foreign exchange, and trade finance accounts with a commercial bank in the Republic of Korea. The representative director and the finance manager are designated as authorized signatories for Swift wire transfers, letters of credit, bank guarantees, and all payment rail instructions. Any payment above a threshold requiring dual signature is subject to two-signatory approval. The bank is authorized to act upon written resolutions approved by the board. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the company is adopted at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation. All statutory notifications, judicial correspondence, and regulatory filings shall be directed to that registered office, and the board directs the representative director to procure and maintain records evidencing exclusive possession or lawful use of such office. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The board appoints the initial representative director, the logistics compliance director, and the anti-money laundering compliance officer. Each appointee accepts office and agrees to act in accordance with the Commercial Act and the company’s internal control policies. The board delegates authority to execute all commercial registration, tax registration, and industrial licensing filings necessary to commence operations. 5. Continuing Delegation. The representative director is authorized to execute all incorporation filings, pay fees, sign leases, open licenses, engage counsel, and carry out all incidental acts required to activate the Yuhan Hoesa. The board confirms these resolutions are binding and effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration and tax compliance onboarding with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the company’s registered office; online filing through the HomeTax electronic filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after completion of commercial registration, apply to the National Tax Service for a business registration certificate. Complete the corporate business registration form stating the legal name, representative director, registered address, principal business activity, and expected date of business commencement. Register for value added tax as a general taxpayer, or apply for tax exemption only if the activity is expressly exempt by Korean tax law. Because the company’s business involves international dangerous goods forwarding, prepare evidence to support zero-rated exported services or VAT refunds where applicable. Register employee withholding accounts, accept appointment notices for the corporate tax card, and file a beneficial ownership disclosure as required under anti-money laundering rules. Maintain the issued business registration certificate as a prerequisite for industrial licensing and opening bank accounts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of commercial registration issued by the court registry
Representative director identity document and power of attorney
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for the registered office
Statement of business activities and expected revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS suspends the registration because of an address mismatch or an incomplete power of attorney, correct the address in the articles or lease, provide a valid power of attorney, and resubmit the application. If issuance is delayed, obtain a receipt from the tax office and escalate to the regional NTS headquarters for administrative remedy, or request a provisional business registration certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation dangerous goods forwarding and industrial licensing application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) freight forwarding registration desk; Ministry of Environment; local municipal Fire and Civil Defense Department; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the statutory international freight forwarding brokerage registration under the International Cargo Transportation Brokerage Act because ISIC 5229 covers specialized forwarding of regulated hazardous chemicals. If the company will physically receive, package, or temporarily store dangerous goods, obtain a hazardous chemical storage or handling permit under the Chemical Substances Control Act and an occupational safety certificate under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Prepare a dangerous goods safety management plan covering segregation, labeling, incident response, and Dangerous Goods Safety Adviser designation. Submit the environmental impact assessment screening or registration as classified by the Ministry of Environment. Obtain a Civil Defense fire safety approval for any warehouse or transfer facility, and ensure that air and sea operations are compliant with IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations and the IMDG Code.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate and commercial registration certificate
Fire safety application and structural load approval
Environmental Impact Assessment or Environmental Registration documents
Dangerous goods safety adviser qualification certificates
Certificate of completion of hazardous materials handling training
Lease or occupancy title for any warehouse or transshipment point
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOLIT, MOE, or the fire authority asks for supplemental information, submit the requested corrections before the stated deadline to keep the application active. If the license application is denied, appeal the denial through the administrative adjudication process or file a judicial appeal with the competent administrative court after curing the identified deficiencies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) Logistics and Maritime Safety Bureau; Ministry of Environment (MOE); local municipal Fire and Civil Defense Department; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Freight Forwarding Brokerage Registration under the International Cargo Transportation Brokerage Act, and Dangerous Goods Forwarding and Hazmat Handling Certificate under the Chemical Substances Control Act and the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) of the Republic of Korea; detailed screening through the Environmental Impact Assessment Support System under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (Simplified EIA) is the applicable classification tier for a dangerous goods forwarding operation without permanent bulk hazardous chemical storage. The tier escalates to a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report where the operation includes warehousing, storage, or transshipment of hazardous chemicals above the statutory thresholds published by the Ministry of Environment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet the Water Environment Conservation Act effluent quality standards, including pH 5.8 to 8.6, BOD not exceeding 50 mg/L, COD not exceeding 50 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 50 mg/L, and total nitrogen and phosphorus limits applicable to public sewer or water body discharge. Volatile organic compound emissions from storage, transfer, mixing, or tank operations must be controlled using vapor recovery systems achieving at least 90 percent capture or recovery efficiency, with ambient VOC concentrations not exceeding the applicable air quality thresholds under the Air Conservation Act. Hazardous waste must be documented on manifests under the Wastes Control Act, stored for no more than six months, and transported, recycled, or disposed of only through MOE-licensed waste treatment facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Completion Certificate issued by the local Civil Defense and Fire Department after inspection of fire extinguishing systems, sprinkler coverage, fire alarms, emergency exits, and dangerous materials storage separation. A structural load inspection certificate from a licensed architect or structural engineer must confirm that any warehouse or transfer facility can support the intended racking and chemical storage loads. Wind, seismic, and workplace safety approvals may be required under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including a KOSHA safety plan approval and permit-to-work system for any DG handling or repackaging area.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must register under Article 8 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act. Application for business registration (including assignment of a tax identification number) is made to the competent district tax office via the HomeTax portal or in person. Required documents: (i) certificate of incorporation or equivalent foreign corporate existence document duly apostilled or certified; (ii) power of attorney and passport/ID of the local agent; (iii) details of the domestic place of business or the authorised agent's details; (iv) written application on the National Tax Service prescribed form. The NTS assigned TIN/VAT registration number is issued within 3 to 5 working days. The same number serves as corporate TIN and VAT ID, and must be disclosed on invoices and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea has no check-the-box or elective pass-through regime for LLCs; all domestic corporations and LLCs are subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Hybrid mismatch adjustments apply under Korean Corporate Tax Act implementing OECD BEPS Action 2, but there is no election mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No mandatory registration threshold; all persons making taxable supplies must register. Simplified taxpayer (simplified VAT) applies to small businesses with annual revenue below KRW 80,000,000, but foreign non-resident entities engaged in taxable supplies are also required to register regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Since 2012, all VAT-registered persons must issue and transmit electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoice) through the HomeTax e-Invoice system in real time. Issuance must occur no later than the day following the supply, and the encrypted digital XML/JSON message must be authenticated under NTS-approved certification. There is no physical clearance stamping; compliance is enforced via real-time API reporting and automated cross-checking of invoice data against VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Articles 21 and 22 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act for (i) export of goods (actual delivery/transport out of Korea); (ii) services performed outside Korea or supplied to a foreign non-resident person; and (iii) international maritime or air transport. For DG (dangerous goods) forwarding, zero-rating applies to freight charges and customs brokerage services attributable to export cargo, provided the underlying movement of goods is lawfully exported under Customs Act procedures and supported by shipping/airway documents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry) filed with Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing international carriage
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Earnings Certificate (foreign currency receipt proof)
Certificate of Origin (if required under the relevant FTA)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False zero-rating claims are subject to penalty tax of 20% of the amount excluded and, in cases of fraud or negligence, 30% to 40% of the VAT evaded; criminal prosecution is possible under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. The NTS may retrospectively claw back zero-rated input tax credits and assess additional VAT on the original supply, plus monthly 0.025% non-payment surcharge for up to 60 months. Documentary insufficiency triggers full disallowance of the export zero-rating benefit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalised current account, with foreign exchange transactions governed by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and delegated to foreign exchange banks. Capital account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment, are generally free but must be reported through designated foreign exchange banks or KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The Korean won (KRW) is convertible for trade and business-related current account flows, but onshore KRW remains restricted in offshore markets; non-residents may not freely open onshore KRW accounts without a permitted economic purpose. Profit remittances are allowed once the company demonstrates tax payment and audited distributable profits, but compliance with foreign exchange reporting, suspected terrorism financing checks, and documentary evidence from the foreign exchange bank is required. There is no surrender requirement for export proceeds, but exporters must collect proceeds within the statutory realisation period, generally 180 days from export declaration, and either deposit them in a foreign currency account with a domestic bank or sell them to a licensed foreign exchange bank. Stringent anti-money laundering screening applies to high-risk dangerous goods forwarding entities, making bank-level convertibility conditional on clean corporate and trade records.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio is in effect. Export proceeds must be received and realised through a licensed foreign exchange bank within 180 days from the date of export declaration; the period may be extended on application for justifiable trade reasons. The proceeds may be held in a domestic foreign-currency deposit account without compulsory KRW conversion, but the bank must be notified and the export collection must be closed in the Electronic Customs Clearance system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Trade Settlement Account
Integrated Capital Escrow and Operating Account
Foreign Investee Capital Escrow Account and Basic KRW Operating Account
Dangerous Goods Trade Settlement Account and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms, including multi-currency e-money wallets and virtual IBAN aggregators without a Korean foreign exchange business licence, are not legally permissible as the primary settlement rail for this entity. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act restricts foreign exchange arbitrage and payment processing to licensed foreign exchange banks; an unlicensed EMI cannot perform cross-border KRW clearing, cannot file Korean foreign exchange reports, and would automatically fail the bank's approved payment account test during the high-risk DG forwarding review. An EMI may be used only as a secondary, low-value disbursement channel if the underlying funds are held with a licensed domestic bank and the EMI has a valid partnership with that bank; primary capital injection and trade payments must remain on SWIFT, MT103, and domestic won wire rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC execution is generally mandatory for foreign-invested high-risk corporations. The statutory directors must appear physically at the designated Korean branch to execute signature cards and confirm the beneficial ownership structure; remote opening is not a standard right. A remote consular proxy opening may be considered only after the bank's AML committee pre-approves the power of attorney, the POA is notarised at a Korean consulate or apostilled, the director's passport and Alien Registration Card or overseas identity are authenticated, and the same sanctions and adverse media screening are completed. In practice, an initial branch interview by the corporate representative or an authorised senior officer with an express board resolution is the fastest compliant path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership chain obscuring the ultimate freight principals in a dangerous goods forwarding entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised corporate registry extract of Yuhan Hoesa, share register, organisational chart showing each intermediate entity, identity and address verification for every beneficial owner above the 10% threshold, passport copies, foreign tax residency certificates, prior-company audited financial statements, sworn explanation of the business rationale for the shareholding structure, and signed management account attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and denied-party exposure from hazardous cargo flows potentially touching embargoed or transit-sensitive jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live denied-party screening reports covering OFAC, EU, UN, and Korean Financial Intelligence Unit lists, customer and supplier screening logs, cargo end-user and end-use certificates, safety data sheets for all DG commodities, export and DG transportation licence from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or National Fire Agency, the approved logistics route list, and contractual bans on re-export to restricted parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual third-party or matching-payment mismatches between LC/MT103 remittances and the actual exporter-beneficiary in the DG freight cycle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised third-party payment deeds, original commercial invoices with matched amounts, bills of lading with consignee confirmation, Korean customs declaration entries, shipping manifests, beneficial economic reason for any interpolation of funds, and a signed representation letter confirming no money-laundering conduit arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory DG forwarder licence or insurance status inadequately documented, creating regulatory risk in the high-risk sector
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid dangerous goods freight forwarding licence or registered logistics operator permit, hazardous materials transport insurance policy, Korea Customs clearance broker registration if acting as customs agent, fire safety and emissions approvals, air waybill/IATA DG handling accreditation or IMDG code sea freight qualification, and a compliance manual with cargo screening procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound investment must be structured under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The foreign investor files a foreign investment report with KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank using the prescribed FDI form; then the capital remittance is wired through SWIFT MT103 using the appropriate purpose code for foreign direct investment from the parent's account to the Yuhan Hoesa capital escrow account in Korea. The receiving bank performs foreign investment verification, accepts the foreign currency, and issues a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. The company completes capital verification from the bank's foreign investment confirmation. The funds must be held in the capital escrow account and later converted to KRW through a licensed bank at the market rate for operational use. All onward transfers require matching underlying invoices or funding plans to avoid violation of foreign exchange verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound settlements from the DG forwarding business, the company should mainly use SWIFT MT103 for general freight invoice payments and agent commissions; commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT710) for overseas payables where bank documentary protection is required; and documentary collections (DP/DA) for smaller, trusted customer relationships. Domestic KRW payments to local carriers, port authorities, and customs duties should be settled on the Korean wire system through the same licensed bank, while foreign currency accounts at the Tier-1 bank handle USD/EUR/JPY clearing. Cargo origin fees, export filing, and charter disbursements should use exact invoice references and DG permits to support the payment field.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contracts (USD/KRW, EUR/KRW, JPY/KRW) with a licensed Korean bank, solely for documented trade receivables or payables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to hedging of the non-convertible KRW exposure with a domestic bank or an offshore counterparty under approved Korean FX documentation, where the underlying trade exposure is proven
Cross-currency swaps and rolling FX swaps permitted only for effective netting of DG forwarding operational cash flows, not for speculative trading
OTC vanilla options or collars permitted on a case-by-case basis when the bank confirms the existence of a real risky underlying trade flow and the maturity matches the freight settlement cycle

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year basis company, by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax amount (reducible to 10% if filed within one month past the statutory deadline), plus daily interest of 0.03% on the overdue tax. Persistent non-filing for three consecutive years may lead to administrative strike-off and forced closure by the court upon NTS or court registry application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report (independent CPA audit report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS); the report must also be submitted to the general shareholders meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the ordinary general shareholders meeting at which the financial statements are approved; the meeting must be held within three months of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by April 14 for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the audit report may result in administrative fines of up to KRW 30 million (approx. USD 23,000) and intensified tax audit scrutiny. Repeated violations may trigger corporate administrative sanctions or audit oversight penalties from the Financial Supervisory Service.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business and Safety Performance Report for Dangerous Goods Freight Forwarding
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) and/or the relevant Korean port/airport authority with jurisdiction over DG forwarding activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year, reporting aggregate weights, dangerous goods classifications, transport routes, and incident logs for the preceding twelve months.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or misreporting may attract an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million (approx. USD 7,500) and suspension of the specialized dangerous goods forwarding license for a period determined by MOLIT. Continued non-compliance can result in permanent revocation of the statutory transportation license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Joint Stock Companies (Korean External Audit Act), an independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory when at least one of the following criteria is met as of the fiscal year-end: (i) total assets exceed KRW 120 billion (approx. USD 93 million); (ii) total assets exceed KRW 70 billion (approx. USD 54 million) and the company's debt-to-equity ratio is at least 150%; (iii) the company is a listed entity, is a financial institution subject to Financial Supervisory Service supervision, or belongs to a corporate group designated for combined audit. A Yuhan Hoesa engaged in DG freight forwarding also becomes subject to compulsory audit if it triggers any of the asset, turnover, or headcount thresholds stipulated in article 4 of the External Audit Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) is the principal accounting framework for all qualified entities subject to external audit. Small and medium-sized enterprises not exceeding the asset thresholds and not required to publish K-IFRS statements may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) according to the SME-specific standards issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants. The financial statements must be prepared in compliance with the Korean Accounting Standards Board (KASB) regulations and the ordinary accounting requirements of the Building and Maintenance of Corporate Books and Financial Records Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not impose a recurring annual UBO confirmation filing for ordinary private limited companies. However, any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership of 25% or more must be registered with the relevant court registry through an amendment registration filed within 30 days from the share transfer or ownership change. For companies executing real estate, large value contracts, or certain AML-sensitive transactions, a concurrent UBO report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU) is required under the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information. The legal representative of the Yuhan Hoesa must verify and preserve UBO updates in the corporate register and update the court records without delay.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (and statutory auditor if appointed)
Register of Charges and Encumbrances (including any mortgages or collateral affecting assets)
Statutory minute book (AGM and board meeting minutes)
Share transfer and beneficial ownership log

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per annum on the Seoul metropolitan market for a professional registered office or corporate secretarial agent service.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 15,000 per annum for the mandatory or voluntary independent audit of a small to mid-sized Yuhan Hoesa engaged in specialized dangerous goods forwarding, depending on transaction volume, statutory consolidation requirements, and the need for K-IFRS compliance.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top national bracket (9%-24% progressive, plus 10% local surtax = 26.4% aggregate top rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified foreign investment enterprises in Free Economic Zones may enjoy 100% corporate income tax exemption for 3 years and 50% for the following 2 years; R&D expense tax credits up to 40%; facility and employment creation credits; no standalone patent box regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Standard Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 1) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for December fiscal year-end, deadline is 31 March of the following year; extension possible with interest on late-paid tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, legal entity name, address, fiscal year end, foreign corporation reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All non-resident shareholders owning 10% or more must be disclosed; attach Tax Residency Certificate and ultimate beneficial ownership details; if Korean management and control are located in Korea, permanent establishment exposure must be assessed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement, balance sheet, notes per K-IFRS with supplementary schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean statutory books must reconcile to intercompany accounting; off-book arrangements are prohibited; DG freight revenue must be supported by bills of lading, customs declarations, and signed logistics contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Gross Revenue and Bad Debt Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from freight forwarding, hazardous materials transport, storage, commission, and incidental logistics services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border revenue and intercompany margins must be set at arm's length; revenue from DG forwarding to a foreign related purchaser cannot be artificially shifted to a low-tax jurisdiction without actual staff and assets in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, charter hire, fuel, port charges, containers, insurance, depreciation, subcontract costs, and restricted entertainment expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident affiliates for management, technical services, or royalty-type charges require true substance, supporting invoices, and contractual delivery; payments lacking proof can be disallowed and recharacterized as constructive dividends subject to withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 22 - Taxable Income and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable base after nondeductible items, tax adjustments, and net operating loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards may be denied if a 50% or greater ownership change occurs without business continuity; a shell DG entity without core income-generating activities in Korea risks full loss disallowance and treaty benefit denial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 26 - Tax Credits and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, special tax credits, CFC income gross-up, and final corporate income tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entity-level foreign tax credits must be calculated source by source; dividend withholding on outbound distribution is not credited on the entity return; DTA reduced withholding is applied by the payer under pre-remittance approval.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% additional tax on the unpaid corporate tax; fraudulent underreporting triggers 40%; other underreporting triggers 10%; unpaid tax carries daily statutory interest; willful tax evasion may be referred under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years and significant fines based on the evaded amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory withholding (20% corporate income tax plus 2% local surtax) on outbound dividends, unless reduced under an applicable Double Tax Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the residence country, complete the HomeTax treaty-relief application through the Korean withholding agent, certify beneficial ownership, demonstrate economic substance and engagement in actual business, and file before remittance; if treaty relief is not pre-approved, excess tax withheld must be reclaimed through a revised return and supporting documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate is 22% for both interest and royalties (20% plus 2% local surtax); DTA rates commonly reduce interest to 0-15% and royalties to 5-15%, but LOB and PPT provisions must be satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory when international related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion per fiscal year; CbC reporting applies when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion or the OECD threshold as implemented.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a standalone ESR/CIGA self-certification regime, but economic substance is enforced through the substance-over-form principle, controlled foreign company rules, General Anti-Avoidance Rules, and treaty anti-abuse provisions; for a DG freight forwarding company, management, personnel, storage, and core income-generating activities must genuinely occur in Korea to preserve deductions and treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Intentional False Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting dangerous-goods freight revenue, fabricating invoices, inflating intercompany expenses, or producing false financial statements to reduce corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty under National Tax Basic Law; criminal prosecution under Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3; imprisonment up to 5 years and fines scaled to the evaded tax; publication of severe tax delinquents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participated in fraud are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and penalties; assets can be attached personally; NTS can impose travel bans and blacklist non-compliant directors; criminal conviction may result in imprisonment and disqualification from corporate management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Transfer Pricing Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a paper Korean entity or low-tax affiliate to route freight forwarding profits, overpay royalties or management fees, or claim treaty benefits without genuine logistics activity, employees, premises, or risk control in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to arm's length result; denial of deductions under Korean TP law; GAAR recapture of tax benefit; additional penalties up to 40% of the understated income; possible CFC inclusion of offshore retained profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil piercing may attach civil liability to directors for confirmed tax deficiencies; directors can be sued for breach of fiduciary duty; overseas travel restriction and criminal exposure arise if the arrangement is treated as deliberate tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Hazardous Goods Operations and AML Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating dangerous-goods forwarding without the required statutory license, deliberately misdeclaring DG cargo, routing proceeds through sanctions-exposed entities, or accepting cash and high-risk payment instruments without proper customer due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of logistics license, trade restrictions, confiscation of illegal profits, administrative fines under the Dangerous Goods Safety Management Act and Foreign Trade Act; criminal referral for wilful non-compliance and financial crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal disqualification from regulated logistics activities, civil damages to shippers and third parties, travel bans, asset freezes, and criminal imprisonment; corporate officers cannot insulate themselves through the limited liability shield when they knowingly breached safety and anti-money-laundering statutes.
